_comment: Each preset combines one of three view ranges with one of five crack-width labels.
delta_c, delta_b and delta_m are voxel-remeshing resolutions in scene units for the
Boolean crack mesh, the bricks affected by Boolean cutting and the mortar mesh.
bevel is the [d_min, d_max] range from which one global bevel depth is sampled.
focal is the [f_min, f_max] range in millimetres used to sample the camera focal length.
The scene is built at scale_factor = 5 scene units per metre-of-wall, so a sampled bevel
value v gives a cutting radius of v * 0.01 scene units, that is 2 * v millimetres, and a
nominal crack width of 4 * v millimetres. The local radius multiplier r_i = r_0 + e_i has
r_0 = 1.0 and e_i ~ U(-0.2, 0.2), so r_i lies in [0.8, 1.2] and the instantaneous width
4 * v * r_i varies by +/-20 per cent along the curve about that nominal value.
Each bevel range is therefore the crack-width label divided by 4: the nominal width spans
exactly the labelled band, and r_i supplies the local variation within a single crack.
Cracks narrower than 3 mm carry no Boolean geometry: they are produced by the procedural
material textures, so their voxel and bevel entries are null.
Differential movement of the two sides of the crack. The wall file records the side
each brick lies on, which allows the two sides to be displaced independently.
Angles are degrees, translations are scene units.
